completion_policy: Complete means the repository has a contract enforcement governance plan, required check definitions, completion gate criteria, archive evidence, and focused validation proving the plan exists. Complete-with-gaps means this track does not itself wire every surface-specific validator into CI, generate every public schema, or enforce every downstream adapter at runtime; dependent surface, release, and package tracks own those implementation-specific gates.

implemented: contract enforcement governance plan in conductor/contract-enforcement.md
required checks for schema drift, fixture conformance, negative conformance, documentation conformance, release conformance, and stub/fake detection
completion gate definitions for versioned contracts, examples, tests, documentation, compatibility notes, and release evidence
archive evidence contract for the harness governance track
not_implemented: every surface-specific validator wired into CI by this track
generated schemas for all public surfaces
release-boundary enforcement for every package registry
runtime validation for downstream adapters outside the repository contracts

gap_register.gap: This track defines the enforcement harness requirements and gate plan; not every surface-specific validator is implemented here.
gap_register.rationale: Surface tracks and release-boundary tracks own their concrete validation commands and CI wiring.

gap_register.gap: Generated-schema and release-boundary drift gates are incomplete for surfaces whose implementation tracks are not locally complete.
gap_register.rationale: Those gates require the corresponding surface contracts, package metadata, or registry workflow to exist before the harness can enforce them.

description: Turn public contracts into generated, validated, drift-checked artifacts across schemas, CLI/file, API, MCP, OpenAI tools, and bindings.
